sentences.text: Heard Shri Dinesh Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the accused/ applicant, Shri Nasiruddin Warsi, learned counsel for the complainant and Shri R.P.Singh learned A.G.A. appearing on behalf of the State respondent.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the accused/ applicant that the accused/applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
He further submitted that in fact the victim was a consenting party and she was major at the time of the incident.
The victim willingly went with the applicant.

In her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., she has stated that she got married Rakesh @ Bulat Gupt vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199520357/
1 with the accused applicant but in her statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C., she has stated that though the applicant enticed her away and she lived with him in a temple and the applicant used to take her to a hotel whenever he wanted to make physical relations.

sentences.text: She has further stated that now the applicant is refusing to marry her.
She has given contradictory statement.
The radiological age of the victim has been found 18 years and she refused for her forensic test, as is evident from Annexure No.4.
The accused applicant is in jail since 10.7.2022.
He has no criminal history, as has been mentioned in paragraph 16 of the affidavit filed alongwith the bail application.
Hence, the applicant be released on bail.

Learned counsel for the private respondent and learned A.G.A. both opposed the bail application and submitted that in the High School Certificate, the date of birth of the victim is mentioned as 1.10.2006 and on the basis of High School Certificate, she is minor and her consent, being minor,
has no meaning in the eyes of law.
Considered the rival submissions made by the parties' counsel and perused the material available on record.

It transpires from perusal of statements of the victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
that she has given contradictory statements.
She remained in a temple for 10 days.
She did not tell anyone during her stay in temple that she is being kept against her wishes.
As per medical examination, the radiological age of the victim has been found 18 years.
Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case as mentioned above, without commenting upon merits, I am of the view that the accused/ applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application filed on behalf of applicant is allowed.

Let the applicant - Rakesh @ Bulat Gupt involved in Case No.143 of 2022 (supra) be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions;
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.

In case of default of this condition,
it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.
